{"cohort_definition": "Final Cohort Definition

1) Index event:
   - Domain: Condition occurrence.
   - Concept set intent: Clinical diagnosis of influenza (influenza-like illness coded as influenza diagnosis). Include only standard SNOMED/standard condition concepts that represent influenza (both seasonal and other influenza viruses). Do not include non-specific respiratory diagnoses (e.g., unspecified viral infection) unless they are mapped to an influenza standard concept.
   - Standard concepts only: Yes.
   - Include descendants: Yes (include all descendant standard condition concepts of the influenza concept set).

2) Entry criteria:
   - Event definition: First qualifying condition occurrence for influenza within the index time window (calendar year 2020).
   - First-ever vs first-in-window: First-in-window with incident washout (see below). Do not require lifetime-first; allow historical diagnoses outside washout for exclusion only.
   - Washout days: Require no influenza condition occurrence in the 365 days prior to the index date (achieve incident-case definition within 365-day clean window).
   - Minimum prior observation: Require at least 365 days of continuous observation prior to the index date.

3) Population constraints:
   - Age at index: Include all ages. (Age at index >= 0 years; no upper age limit.)
   - Sex: Include all sexes.
   - Additional inclusion filters: None.
   - Note on grouping: Analysis will stratify by age groups (see Notes/Assumptions for recommended bands). Grouping is an analysis step and not an entry filter.

4) Visit/setting restrictions:
   - None. Include influenza condition occurrences recorded in any care setting (outpatient, emergency department, inpatient) unless the data source maps the condition only to a specific visit; do not require a visit type for inclusion.

5) Time window for index:
   - Allowed index dates: 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31 inclusive (calendar year 2020).

6) Exclusions:
   - Prior conditions/exposures/procedures: Exclude individuals who have an influenza condition occurrence in the 365 days prior to the index date (this is handled by washout/incident requirement above).
   - Pregnancy, COVID-19 co-infection, asymptomatic cases, or care-setting exclusions: None specified; do not exclude for these unless specified later.

7) Cohort exit:
   - Cohort end date: Index date (end of day = same date). The cohort represents the event occurrence on the index date.
   - Episode/deduplication rules: Limit to a single index event per person during the index time window (calendar year 2020). If a person has multiple qualifying influenza condition occurrences in 2020, select the first occurrence that satisfies the 365-day prior-observation requirement.

8) Notes/assumptions:
   - Assumption: The user requested a "rate" measure; this cohort is defined for incident-case counts during 2020 (incidence within calendar year 2020). Rate computation (numerator/denominator, person-time) will be performed downstream in analysis; this cohort provides incident events for counting/analysis.
   - Assumption: Incident cases are defined using a 365-day washout prior to index. This conservative default is chosen because the user did not specify washout length.
   - Assumption: Minimum prior observation required is 365 days to reliably apply the washout. Individuals with <365 days prior observation are excluded.
   - Assumption: Index uses condition occurrences only. Lab-confirmed influenza identified solely by measurement codes (e.g., positive PCR) are not included unless they are represented as a condition occurrence in the source data or the concept set is expanded to include measurement-based definitions. If lab-confirmed-only cases are desired, add measurement concept set with value indicating positive result and include as additional index criteria.
   - Assumption: Use standard concepts (OMOP standard vocabulary); include descendants to capture specific influenza subtypes and related influenza diagnosis codes mapped under the influenza concept set.
   - Assumption: No visit-type restriction to maximize capture across care settings; if only hospitalized cases are desired, add a requirement that the condition occurrence is associated with an inpatient visit.
   - Recommended age groups for downstream stratified rate reporting (not applied as filters): 0–4, 5–17, 18–49, 50–64, 65+ years.
   - Implementation note: In ATLAS, create a condition concept set named clearly (e.g., "Influenza (standard concepts, include descendants)") and use the cohort entry rule: first condition occurrence during 2020, with 365 days prior continuous observation and no prior influenza condition in the 365 days before index. Set cohort end to index date and limit to earliest event per person during the calendar year.

End of definition.", "refinement_feedback": ""}
